key_points: Meta's Muse AI agent is sparking fears of structural disruption to online travel agencies by reducing 'consumer inertia' that benefits platforms like Booking.com, causing sentiment-driven selling
BKNG declined ~2.5-4% in a single session, but the move appears narrative/rotation-driven rather than reflecting any change to near-term fundamentals or earnings
Institutional investors (Andra AP fonden, State Street) were accumulating shares on the dip, suggesting some market participants view the selloff as overdone

Long-term AI disruption risk warrants monitoring but Booking Holdings has significant competitive moats including brand strength, loyalty programs, supply-side relationships, and its own AI capabilities
Key near-term catalyst to watch: Muse's actual adoption rate among consumers and any visible impact on OTA booking volumes or take rates
